scope: Desktop/client Create recovery plus durable server-side rejection receipts; no new physical VM or provider task.
regressions: Discard accepted acknowledgement, reopen client and database, return the same VM/operation at full quota.
Eight concurrent independent database connections replay one accepted key.
Persist rejection across database reopen and quota growth; reject changed payload and legacy delayed copies.
Injected application admission failure rolls back VM, CPU, network and application claims before the rejection commits.
Real QUIC sends Create, waits for commit, closes without reading, reconnects and replays one VM.
Revoked-device errors remain generic errors rather than definitive creation rejection.
Corrupt/mismatched journals and competing windows fail closed.
Late or mismatched replies do not resolve another key or alter another VM editor.
Confirmation dialog remains actionable at full quota/offline observation and retains its dismissal body.
limits: Fault-injection tests use temporary databases and simulated host execution; the dropped-response transport test uses real local QUIC.
This does not change or validate hotspot connectivity, off-host backup durability, or all underlying Incus/QEMU lifecycle interleavings.
Do not discard unresolved journals or server rejection receipts while delayed requests may replay.
